thesis: Rewarding the steps of studying and reasoning, not just the final answer, raised proof accuracy far more than retrieval alone.
rationale: The two bars show exactly what the caption claims: proof accuracy rose from 51.5% to 79.5% once the model was rewarded for the steps of studying and reasoning rather than only the final answer, making the fine-grained-reward argument legible at a glance.
title: Fine-Grained Rewards *Lift* Proof Accuracy
subhead: Rewarding the study process beats scoring only the final answer

chart.source: Source: Kong et al., BookNavigator study
